Khodeja Begum & others ------ Petitioner
vs.

full_judgment:
12. The learned Advocate submits that the defendants denied the marriage in their clear and specific pleadings in the written statement. He submits that the plaintiff in order to prove the marriage submitted a forged Kabinnama Exhibit 1 but the register of marriage, the Marriage Registrar as well as the witnesses of the marriage were not examined and there is no signature of the defendant No.1 in Exhibit 1 and therefore it was not legally proved under sections 61 and 67 of the Evidence Act and the same can not be, a proof of the marriage of the plaintiff with the defendant No.1. He submits that there is specific assertion of the defendants in their pleadings that there was no marriage between the plaintiff and the defendant No.1. In such circumstances the burden of proof lies on the plaintiff to prove the marriage and the Kabinnama Exhibit 1 which is under challenge was not proved. He submits that the alleged compromise deal (Exhibit-3) dated 21-8-81 between the plaintiff and the defendant No.1 to live together as husband and wife was not proved under section 67 of the Evidence Act as the same was denied by the defendant No.1 and no witness of the deal was examined. He submits that by mis-construction and misreading of the alleged documents Exhibit 1 and Exhibit 4 the lower appellate Court reversed the judgment of the trial Court on the basis of those exhibits which were not legally proved. The learned Advocate further submits that the decree is in executable as it is a relationship between a man and a woman and the Constitution of Bangladesh also guarantees equality and liberty of each irrespective of man and woman, caste or creed, etc. 

 14. I heard the learned Advocates of both sides, perused the petitions and the records. The Exhibit 1, the Kabinnama shows there is no signature of the bride and the learned Advocate for the opposite party submits that it is not very material that the signature of the bride should be also in the copy. But it is a most important document of proof of marriage between the petitioner No.1 and the opposite Party No.1 and the burden lies upon the plaintiff-opposite party to prove the Kabinnama but he did not take it seriously to prove the same. The original marriage register was not brought before the court nor the marriage registrar or the witnesses in the marriage who allegedly signed in the Kabinnama were examined. 

 15. The Muslim marriage is a socio-religious contract and the signatures of both the parties are very essential to prove the contract of marriage written in the form of Kabinnama. In such circumstances no amount of oral evidence will cure the deficiency and no amount of oral evidence will be sufficient to prove the marriage when the plaintiff failed to prove the Kabinnama according to law. In such circumstances the marriage was not proved which is denied in the pleadings of the defendant in her written statement. It is alleged that a compromise deal was executed on 21-8-1991 (Exhibit-3) between the plaintiff and the defendant No.1 regarding their marriage and the same was filed I before the Court, by the plaintiff. The defendant No.1 flatly denied her marriage with the plaintiff and the compromise deal so here also burden of proof lies on the plaintiff to prove the same but he did not examine the alleged witnesses who signed the compromise deal and the court also did not examine the plaintiff and the defendant in respect of this compromise to come to a conclusion that the same was executed by both plaintiff am the defendant No.1 and marked as Exhibit 3. 

 16. The similar is the case of the divorce I notice allegedly sent by the defendant No.1 on 25-3-1981, the Exhibit 4 and same also was not I proved by the plaintiff. Thus, in view of the total denial of marriage by the defendant with the plaintiff and plaintiffs failure to prove, Exhibits 1, 3 and 4 under sections 61, 67 and 103 of the Evidence Act, the same can not be accepted as documents of proof of marriage and the learned lower appellate Court due to misreading and mis-construction of the documents (Exhibits 1, 3 and 4) in proving the marriage according to the provisions of Evidence Act, the findings of marriage are illegal and the pleadings of the defendant No.1 that there was no marriage of the defendant with the plaintiff is established.
